title: Not a fan of all the additional nonsense.
body:
Spotify has completely lost the plot. I’m paying for a music app, not a bloated entertainment platform trying to force podcasts, videos, clips, and endless features I never asked for. The app used to be simple: open Spotify, play music, discover music. Now it’s slow, cluttered, frustrating, and honestly exhausting to navigate.

As a longtime music lover, I spend more time trying to FIND my playlists than actually listening to music. There are too many tabs, too many distractions, and too many unnecessary features getting in the way of the core experience. I use Spotify daily at the gym and when I’m on the move — I don’t have time to scroll through a maze of content just to play an album or playlist.

The app performance has noticeably gotten worse too. Everything feels heavier and slower because Spotify is trying to do too much at once. It’s become so overcomplicated that I literally bought a vintage iPod just to enjoy music again without frustration.

Spotify needs to remember why people fell in love with the platform in the first place: MUSIC. Not podcasts. Not video feeds. Not TikTok-style content. Music discovery used to feel effortless and exciting. Now opening the app just irritates me.

The company seriously needs more real-world user testing focused on usability and simplicity because from a user experience standpoint, this app has become cluttered and stressful. If it weren’t bundled with Hulu, I would’ve already canceled my subscription.

title: Lag
body:
For over a week now every single button press has been a hassle. Simply “liking” a song, searching for one, or adding one to a playlist takes forever. Artist pages and album track lists take take ages to fully load. And then on top of all that, there’s a 50/50 chance of the app crashing in the middle of it or nothing loading at all other than the “currently unavailable” message. 

I admit, my “liked songs” list is massive. But as far as I’m aware, there isn’t a limit for a reason - I know there used to be a 10,000 song cap, and while I wasn’t a fan of that I’d rather Spotify had kept it if it was going to be incapable of handling more. I really don’t know what the problem could be other than this. I would attempt to remove songs and put them in separate playlists if that would help, but I’m not sure if it even would considering I’d still have the same amount of data being stored on my profile. 

Anyway, just wanted to put this out there in case anyone else is experiencing this so they know they aren’t the only one.

title: Broke wireless CarPlay for ugly logo change
body:
Spotify managed to break wireless CarPlay functionality in my Ford F-150 immediately after pushing the latest update with the new disco ball UI/logo changes.

Before this update, everything worked perfectly. Now the app constantly displays the wrong track on CarPlay, usually one song behind, while the audio itself continues normally. I spent hours troubleshooting:
- deleted and reinstalled Spotify
- cleared cache
- removed and re-paired CarPlay
- rebooted Ford SYNC
- reset Bluetooth connections
- restarted phone multiple times

Nothing fixed it.

Meanwhile YouTube Music works perfectly on the exact same wireless CarPlay setup, and Spotify works correctly when plugged in wired. That clearly points to Spotify breaking wireless CarPlay metadata handling in this latest update.

Even more frustrating is that this appears to have been pushed primarily for an unnecessary and honestly hideous disco ball UI refresh that many users did not ask for.

Please focus less on cosmetic redesigns and more on maintaining stable core functionality for paying users.
